claims.standfirst: Food dropped on the floor picks up bacteria immediately. The rule is a joke that got studied.

claims.title: The Flannan Isles Lighthouse
claims.standfirst: Three lighthouse keepers vanished from a Hebridean island in 1900. The lamps were trimmed, the kitchen was abandoned mid-meal, and no bodies were found.

claims.title: Flat Earth & the Firmament
claims.standfirst: A disc with the North Pole at the centre, a wall of ice at the rim, and a dome overhead. The model is simple. What is interesting is how it survives.

facts.Core components: Disc · ice rim · dome · spotlight sun
facts.Fatal objection: Gravity on a disc pulls to the centre
facts.Related: Ice Wall, Hollow Earth, Dual Suns

claims.title: The Flatwoods Monster
claims.standfirst: A group in West Virginia reported a tall figure with a red face and a hood after seeing a light in the sky. The most economical explanation is a meteor and an owl.

claims.title: The Fleshgait and the Wendigo
claims.standfirst: Two creatures from different traditions, run together on the internet. One is an internet invention; the other belongs to Algonquian peoples.

claims.title: Flexible Glass
claims.theme: The ancient world, myth and archaeology
claims.standfirst: The story of a glass that could be bent, and an inventor executed to protect the gold trade. It is a legend with no evidence.

claims.title: Flint's Lead
claims.standfirst: A city switched its water source to save money, and the water corroded the pipes. The lead poisoning is documented.

claims.title: Noah, Gilgamesh & the Great Flood
claims.standfirst: A man builds a boat, loads the animals, and the world is drowned. The story is older than the Bible, and the geology is younger than the story.

facts.Oldest flood epic: Gilgamesh XI, from c. 1750 BC material

claims.title: The Flores Hobbit's Ancestry
claims.standfirst: Homo floresiensis is accepted as a species; where it came from is still argued.

claims.title: Fluoride and the Pineal Gland
claims.standfirst: The claim that water fluoridation calcifies the pineal gland and dulls the mind. The studies cited are high-dose animal work, and the doses are orders of magnitude above drinking water.

claims.title: The Flynn Effect
claims.standfirst: Measured intelligence rose by about three points a decade through the twentieth century, in every country with good data. Then, in several of them, it stopped. Both halves of that sentence are strange.

facts.Named for: James Flynn, who described it in 1984
facts.Size: About 3 IQ points a decade; ~15–20 over the century
facts.Where the gain sits: Abstract reasoning, not vocabulary or arithmetic
facts.Reversal: Reported since the 1990s in several rich countries

claims.title: The FNAF Dream Theory
claims.standfirst: The theory that the whole game series is a child's dream. It was popular, it was abandoned by the community, and the creator denied it.

claims.title: Folie à Deux
claims.standfirst: A delusion shared by two people in a close relationship, usually one dominant and one suggestible. It is rare, it is real, and the modern diagnostic manuals have quietly stopped calling it a separate illness.

facts.Structure: Inducer and recipient, in a close relationship
facts.Modern status: Folded into the schizophrenia spectrum in DSM-5

claims.title: Forensic fMRI
claims.standfirst: The claim that brain scans can detect lies or memories. The research exists; the courtroom use does not.

claims.title: The Four Humours
claims.standfirst: Two thousand years of medicine built on four bodily fluids. It was wrong, and it was wrong in a way that made sense.

claims.title: FRBs as Light Sails
claims.standfirst: Fast radio bursts are real and unexplained. The proposal that they are alien light sails is the weakest of the options.

claims.title: The Free Energy Principle
claims.standfirst: A single mathematical principle is said to explain perception, action, learning and life itself. Its defenders call it the closest thing neuroscience has to a unifying law; its critics call it unfalsifiable, and both have a point.

facts.Author: Karl Friston, from 2006
facts.Core quantity: Variational free energy (a bound on surprise)
facts.Empirical record: Active inference works; the grand claim is untested

claims.title: The French Paradox
claims.standfirst: A country with high saturated fat and low heart disease. The explanation is still argued.

facts.Observation: Low heart disease despite fat intake

claims.title: The Fresno Nightcrawlers
claims.standfirst: A night-vision video showed two pale, walking figures with no arms or head. The best explanation is a deer seen from behind, at night, at an odd angle.

facts.Description: Pale, walking, no visible head or arms

claims.title: Frozen, Tangled and Tarzan
claims.standfirst: The theory that Tarzan is Anna and Elsa's brother, shipwrecked as a baby. It rests on a ship, a timeline and a set of parents who look similar.

facts.Theory: Tarzan is Anna and Elsa's brother

claims.title: FTX's Backdoor
claims.standfirst: An exchange took customer deposits and lent them to a related trading firm, using a hidden exemption in its accounting. It collapsed in days.

claims.title: FTX
claims.standfirst: Billions in customer deposits were lent to a trading firm run by the founder's girlfriend, moved through code exemptions, and spent on venture bets and real estate.

facts.Mechanism: Customer funds to Alameda; code backdoor

claims.title: Why We Lost Our Fur
claims.standfirst: Humans are the naked ape: hairless, sweaty, and able to run in heat. The three leading explanations are thermoregulation, parasites and sexual selection, and the fossil evidence does not choose between them.

facts.What changed: Hair became fine and short; follicle density unchanged

claims.title: Fusion on the Grid
claims.standfirst: In December 2022 the National Ignition Facility got more energy out of a fusion target than the laser delivered. Headlines said fusion had arrived. The grid is still waiting.

claims.title: Gadget Is a Decoy
claims.standfirst: The theory that Inspector Gadget is a decoy while his niece does the work. It is a joke about the show's structure, and the show's structure supports it.

claims.title: Gaia, Weak and Strong
claims.standfirst: The proposal that life regulates the planet's conditions. The weak version is mainstream; the strong version is not.

claims.title: Gaia
claims.label_text: A metaphor that became a science
claims.standfirst: The Earth regulates its own temperature, chemistry and atmosphere as if it were alive. The strong version is wrong, the weak version is now mainstream, and the argument between them created Earth system science.

claims.title: The Ganzfeld Effect
claims.standfirst: Put half ping-pong balls over someone's eyes, play white noise, and within minutes most people start to hallucinate. The effect is real; the parapsychology built on top of it is not.

facts.Onset: Vivid imagery within minutes for most people
facts.Cause: Removal of structure from sensory input

claims.title: Gaster, Erased
claims.standfirst: A character in Undertale who exists only in fragments of the game's code and lore. The fragments are real; the character is a designed mystery.

claims.title: The Gate of the Sun
claims.theme: The ancient world, myth and archaeology
claims.standfirst: A monolithic gate at Tiwanaku carries a carved figure holding staffs, surrounded by winged attendants. It is a real monument with a documented iconography, and it has been read as a calendar, a portal and a record of visitors.

claims.title: Gateway of the Mind
claims.standfirst: A creepypasta about a sensory deprivation experiment that goes wrong. It is written as a case report, and the report is the fiction.

claims.title: The Gateway Process
claims.standfirst: A 1983 CIA report describes consciousness as a hologram and out-of-body travel as a change in brainwave frequency. It is a literature review written by one officer, and it is cited as though it were a finding.

claims.title: Gemini Home Entertainment
claims.standfirst: An analog horror series presented as a catalogue of home videos about nature, which turns out to be about something else.

claims.title: Genes Jumping Between Animals
claims.standfirst: Genes that move between species, not just from parent to child. Horizontal transfer is documented; its importance is argued.

claims.title: Genghis Khan's Burial
claims.theme: The ancient world, myth and archaeology
claims.standfirst: The khan asked to be buried without a mark, and the location has been secret for eight centuries. Searches have been conducted, and the Mongolian government has stopped them.

claims.title: Geographic Determinism
claims.standfirst: Eurasia has more domesticable plants, more large animals and a long east–west axis. That is true and important. Whether it explains which countries are rich today is another question.

claims.title: Geopolymer Pyramids
claims.theme: The ancient world, myth and archaeology
claims.standfirst: A French chemist proposed that the pyramid's blocks were cast from a limestone geopolymer rather than quarried. The idea explains some odd features and is contradicted by others, and the argument has been running for forty years.

facts.Evidence against: Quarry marks, tool marks, continuous sedimentary fabric

claims.title: The Georgia Guidestones
claims.standfirst: A granite monument in Georgia carried ten commandments for a post-apocalyptic age, in eight languages. It was commissioned anonymously, vandalised repeatedly, and destroyed by a bomb in 2022.

claims.title: Gesture or Voice First
claims.standfirst: Did language begin in the hands or the mouth? The evidence is indirect, and the debate has moved with discoveries about mirror systems, sign languages and ape gestures.

claims.title: The Giant Squid
claims.theme: The ancient world, myth and archaeology
claims.standfirst: A deep-sea animal known from carcasses and beaks for centuries, filmed alive only in 2004.

claims.title: The Giant Trees
claims.standfirst: Devils Tower does look like a stump. It has vertical grain, a flat top and a flared base. It is also made of a rock that trees cannot make.

facts.Related: Giants, Young-Earth claims, Expansion and gigantism

claims.title: Giants
claims.standfirst: There is a race of giants in the oldest stories we have. There is also a ten-foot gypsum corpse in a New York field, sold for $23,000, and a mastodon thigh-bone that looked like a man.

facts.Related: Titans, Giants in fossil beds, Scale claims

claims.title: Gilgamesh's Tomb
claims.theme: The ancient world, myth and archaeology
claims.standfirst: A claim that the tomb of Gilgamesh was found under the Euphrates. The structure is real; the identification is a reading.

claims.title: The Giraffe's Neck
claims.standfirst: Lamarck's favourite example is not a Lamarckian one. The neck has seven vertebrae, like yours, and the best explanation is not that giraffes stretched.

facts.Leading hypothesis: Sexual selection, with feeding as a secondary pressure
facts.Fossil record: Intermediate necks in Samotherium and relatives
facts.Open question: Why the count stays at seven

claims.title: The Giza Power Plant
claims.theme: The ancient world, myth and archaeology
claims.standfirst: The claim that the Great Pyramid was a machine for generating electricity, with the King's Chamber as a resonant cavity. It is an engineering hypothesis with no artefact of any machine in it.

facts.Claim: The pyramid generated and transmitted power
facts.Required: Coils, conductors, insulators, a working fluid
facts.The real precision: Explained by surveying and long practice

claims.title: The Glass Transition
claims.standfirst: Liquids cooled into glass never crystallise, and nobody has a complete theory of why. It is a real, everyday unsolved problem.

claims.title: The Gleiwitz Incident
claims.standfirst: German agents staged an attack on a radio station and blamed Poland, as the pretext for invasion. Prisoners were killed and left as 'casualties'.

claims.title: The Global Consciousness Project
claims.standfirst: A network of random number generators, said to deviate from randomness when large numbers of people are emotionally engaged. The statistics do not survive the way the events were chosen.

claims.title: Göbekli Tepe
claims.standfirst: Carved pillars, sixteen tonnes each, built by people without pottery or farming. The date is settled. What the enclosures were for is not.

claims.title: The Gold Standard
claims.standfirst: Money redeemable in gold, praised for discipline and blamed for depression. The history is documented; the lesson is argued.

claims.title: The Goldbach Conjecture
claims.standfirst: Every even number greater than two is the sum of two primes. It has been checked to four quintillion and proved for nobody.

facts.Statement: Every even n > 2 is the sum of two primes

claims.title: The Goldfish Memory Myth
claims.standfirst: The claim that fish forget everything in three seconds. Experiments show learning that lasts months.

claims.title: Goodhart's Law
claims.standfirst: When a measure becomes a target, it stops being a good measure. The law is a one-line summary of a century of institutional failure, and it is demonstrated every year.

facts.Mechanism: Optimising the proxy instead of the goal
facts.Examples: Soviet quotas; Wells Fargo; NHS targets

claims.title: The Google Effect
claims.standfirst: People remember where to find information rather than the information itself. The 2011 paper that named it is famous; the replications are mixed, which is the honest state of the finding.

claims.title: Gorillas
claims.theme: The ancient world, myth and archaeology
claims.standfirst: A great ape described by Western science in 1847, and known to the peoples who lived beside it for far longer.

claims.title: The Gospel of Judas
claims.theme: The ancient world, myth and archaeology
claims.standfirst: A Gnostic gospel in which Judas is asked to betray Jesus. The manuscript is real, and it was published and then conserved.

claims.title: Grabby Aliens
claims.standfirst: A model in which civilisations expand at a fixed speed and announce themselves, and the fact that we see none constrains when they appear. It explains the Fermi paradox by predicting we are early.

facts.Prediction: We are early; arrival far in the future

claims.title: The Grail Bloodline
claims.theme: The ancient world, myth and archaeology
claims.standfirst: The claim that the Holy Grail is not a cup but a bloodline, descending from Jesus, and that a secret society has guarded it. The society was invented in 1956, and its documents were forgeries.

claims.title: The Grand Canyon Citadel
claims.theme: The ancient world, myth and archaeology
claims.standfirst: A newspaper story about an ancient citadel in the Grand Canyon, with Egyptian and Tibetan artefacts. It was a hoax.

claims.title: The Grandmother Hypothesis
claims.standfirst: Human females live decades past childbearing, which is rare among mammals. The proposal is that grandmothers helped feed weaned children, and that this is why menopause exists.

claims.title: Graphology
claims.standfirst: The claim that handwriting reveals personality. It has been tested many times and does not work.

claims.title: Gravity in Tabletop Experiments
claims.standfirst: Experiments small enough for a laboratory bench now probe gravity itself. The measurements are real and the anomalies are not.

claims.title: The Great Attractor
claims.standfirst: Galaxies across a wide region flow toward something in the direction of Centaurus, and for two decades nobody could see what. The answer turned out to be larger than the thing they were looking for.

facts.Direction: Centaurus / Norma, behind the galactic plane
facts.Current picture: Laniakea: a local basin in a larger flow

claims.title: The Great Filter
claims.standfirst: The silence has to mean something. Either the hard step is behind us and we are lucky, or it is ahead of us and we are early.

facts.Claim: At least one step is very improbable

claims.title: The Great Martian God
claims.standfirst: A 1976 Viking image showed a face on Mars. Higher-resolution images showed a mesa. The claim survived the picture, which is the interesting part.

facts.Afterlife: Claims the new images were doctored

claims.title: The Great Oxidation Event
claims.standfirst: About 2.4 billion years ago the atmosphere filled with oxygen, the planet froze, and most of the life then living died. The evidence is in rocks that record the moment the air changed.

facts.Open: How high oxygen actually rose, and for how long

claims.title: The Great Stagnation
claims.standfirst: The postwar generation got antibiotics, electrification, cars and mass higher education. Since 1970 the measurable productivity dividend has been much thinner — or the measurement has stopped counting what matters.

facts.Strongest pessimist case: Gordon, The Rise and Fall of American Growth

claims.title: Greek Fire
claims.theme: The ancient world, myth and archaeology
claims.standfirst: A Byzantine incendiary that burned on water and was projected from ships. The recipe was a state secret, and it was kept: nobody knows exactly what it was.

claims.title: The Green Children of Woolpit
claims.theme: The ancient world, myth and archaeology
claims.standfirst: Two children with green skin and an unknown language appeared in a Suffolk village in the twelfth century. The story is in two chronicles, and the explanations on offer are all more ordinary than the story.

facts.Sources: William of Newburgh; Ralph of Coggeshall

claims.title: The Green Coffee Bean Scam
claims.standfirst: A weight-loss supplement promoted on television with a study that was retracted and a researcher who was paid.

claims.title: The Green Run
claims.standfirst: A secret test released radioactive material over Washington state to see how it would disperse. It was detected 300 km away, and the public was told nothing.

claims.title: Grey Goo
claims.standfirst: Self-replicating nanobots that consume the biosphere. It comes from a 1986 book about molecular manufacturing, and the physics of building it has never been demonstrated.

facts.Key objection: Mechanosynthesis does not work in wet, warm conditions
facts.Drexler's own view: Unlikely; a distraction from real risks

claims.title: The Grievance Studies Affair
claims.standfirst: A team submitted deliberately absurd papers to humanities journals; several were accepted. The episode is documented and contested.

claims.title: The Griffin and Protoceratops
claims.standfirst: A suggestion that the griffin's shape comes from fossil dinosaur skeletons in Central Asia. The fossils are there; the transmission is a guess.

claims.title: Group versus Kin Selection
claims.standfirst: Why do animals help each other? Hamilton's rule explains a lot, and the argument about group selection has never quite ended.

claims.title: Growth Mindset
claims.standfirst: Believing that ability can grow is a defensible idea with a small, real effect. Believing it is a lever that raises attainment for everyone is a claim that failed its largest test.

facts.National trial: Yeager et al., 2019: ~12,000 students, near-zero average
facts.What changed: Effect sizes shrank as samples grew

claims.title: GTA's Two Universes
claims.standfirst: The Grand Theft Auto games are split into a 3D universe and an HD universe, with separate continuities. Rockstar confirmed it, and it explains why the same city looks different.

facts.3D universe: GTA III, Vice City, San Andreas

claims.title: The Guatemala Syphilis Experiments
claims.standfirst: US researchers deliberately infected Guatemalan soldiers, prisoners and psychiatric patients with syphilis to test penicillin. The subjects were not told, and the study was hidden for sixty years.

claims.title: Gunung Padang
claims.theme: The ancient world, myth and archaeology
claims.standfirst: A terraced hill in Indonesia was claimed in 2023 to be a 25,000-year-old pyramid. Geologists and archaeologists have challenged the dating and the interpretation.

facts.2023 claim: A layered pyramid from 25,000 years ago
facts.Criticism: Cores and dates do not support construction

claims.title: The Gut–Brain Axis
claims.standfirst: Gut bacteria talk to the brain, and the brain talks back. The question is how much of the conversation changes disease, and how much is a passenger effect.

claims.title: HAARP Weather Control
claims.standfirst: A research facility in Alaska heats a patch of the upper atmosphere with radio waves. It has been blamed for earthquakes, hurricanes and mind control, and its power output is smaller than a large city's.

claims.title: Hair Comparison
claims.standfirst: FBI examiners testified that hairs 'matched' a suspect. The testimony overstated what the method could do.

claims.title: Hair and Nails After Death
claims.standfirst: Hair and nails do not grow after death. The skin recedes and creates the illusion.

facts.Claim: Hair and nails grow after death

claims.title: The Hall of Records
claims.theme: The ancient world, myth and archaeology
claims.standfirst: A chamber beneath the Sphinx, said to hold the records of Atlantis, predicted by a psychic. Seismic surveys and excavations have found nothing.

claims.title: The Handicap Principle
claims.standfirst: The proposal that costly signals are honest precisely because they are costly. It explains a lot and is hard to test.

claims.title: The Hanging Munchkin
claims.standfirst: A shadow in The Wizard of Oz is said to be a Munchkin actor who hanged himself on set. It is a bird, and the story has been checked many times.

facts.Claim: A hanging visible in a shot
facts.Reality: A large bird used on set

claims.title: Harvest Now, Decrypt Later
claims.standfirst: Encrypted traffic is being recorded today so it can be read when quantum computers are able to break the encryption. It is not a theory about the future; it is guidance from the agencies, and a migration that is already under way.

claims.title: Havana Syndrome
claims.standfirst: Diplomats in Havana reported headaches, dizziness and cognitive problems, and some heard a sound. Eight years of investigation have produced two rival explanations and no confirmed cause.

claims.title: Heritability of Intelligence
claims.standfirst: Twin and adoption studies put the heritability of adult IQ high. What that number means, and what it does not, is where the argument lives.

claims.title: Hero's Steam Engine
claims.theme: The ancient world, myth and archaeology
claims.standfirst: A sphere turned by steam, described by Hero of Alexandria. It is a real device and it was not used for work.

claims.title: Did Hitler Escape?
claims.standfirst: A U-boat to Argentina, a Nazi compound in Patagonia, a death staged in the bunker. The story has books, documentaries and declassified FBI files. It does not have a body that matches.

claims.title: The Hittites
claims.theme: The ancient world, myth and archaeology
claims.standfirst: An empire mentioned in the Bible, recovered from a Turkish mound with an archive of cuneiform tablets.

claims.title: The Hodge Conjecture
claims.standfirst: A statement about which shapes can be described by equations. It is one of the hardest open problems in mathematics and one of the least explainable.

claims.title: The Hohokam Collapse
claims.standfirst: A desert society built hundreds of kilometres of canals, then abandoned them. The cause is argued.

claims.title: Hollow Earth & the Inner Sun
claims.standfirst: The shell has an 800-mile wall. The polar openings are 1,400 miles wide. There is a small sun in the middle, and someone has always just come back from there.

facts.Fatal objection: Seismic wave paths and mean density

claims.title: The Holobiont Human
claims.standfirst: You are a habitat: trillions of microbes, thousands of species, and a genome many times larger than yours. The holobiont concept treats the human and its microbes as one unit, and it is now standard.

facts.Cells: Roughly one to one microbial to human
facts.Evidence type: Mostly correlational outside a few cases

claims.title: Holographic Noise
claims.standfirst: If space is a hologram, it should jitter at the Planck scale. A purpose-built interferometer looked for the jitter and found nothing, which ruled out some versions of the idea.

claims.title: The Holographic Principle
claims.standfirst: The information in a volume of space can be encoded on its boundary. In one kind of universe, this has been demonstrated. Whether it applies to ours is open.

claims.title: Homeopathy in India
claims.standfirst: The largest homeopathy market in the world, and the evidence base it rests on.

claims.title: Homo floresiensis
claims.standfirst: A metre-tall hominin found on Flores, dated to as recently as 50,000 years ago. The discovery was disputed for a decade and is now accepted.

claims.title: The Hopi Ant People
claims.theme: The ancient world, myth and archaeology
claims.standfirst: Hopi tradition describes ancestors sheltering underground with the Ant People during a world's destruction. It is a sacred narrative, and the reading that makes it an account of extraterrestrial rescue is an outsider's.

facts.The Ant People: Beings who shelter and teach the ancestors
facts.Community response: Objection to the use of the tradition

claims.title: The Hopkinsville Goblins
claims.standfirst: A family in Kentucky reported a siege by small silver figures after a light in the sky. The case is well documented and the leading explanation is owls.

claims.title: The Horizon Scandal
claims.standfirst: A faulty accounting system made subpostmasters look like thieves. Hundreds were prosecuted, some went to prison, and the Post Office fought the victims for twenty years.

claims.title: How Modern Humans Spread
claims.standfirst: Out of Africa, with interbreeding and multiple dispersals. The broad picture is settled and the details are not.

claims.title: The Hubble Tension
claims.standfirst: Measure the expansion of the universe nearby and you get 73. Measure it in the early universe and you get 67. Both teams are careful, both error bars are small, and the gap is now five sigma.

claims.title: The Hygiene Hypothesis
claims.standfirst: The proposal that too-clean childhoods leave the immune system under-trained. The epidemiology is suggestive and the mechanism is argued.

claims.title: Zimbabwe's Hyperinflation
claims.standfirst: A currency destroyed by printing, with documented causes and documented consequences.

claims.title: Hyperloop Feasibility
claims.standfirst: The white paper was 57 pages of enthusiasm. The hard parts were not the magnets; they were the tube, the thermal expansion, the safety case and the fact that a train needs to carry enough people to pay for itself.

claims.title: Hypernormalisation
claims.standfirst: Adam Curtis's argument that politics has become a managed spectacle. It is a documentary essay, and it is argued as one.

claims.title: The Hypogeum Oracle Room
claims.theme: The ancient world, myth and archaeology
claims.standfirst: A subterranean chamber in Malta that resonates at a specific frequency. The acoustics are measured; the ritual use is inferred.

claims.title: Hysteria
claims.standfirst: A diagnosis applied to women for two thousand years, and removed from the manuals in 1980.

claims.title: The Ica Stones
claims.theme: The ancient world, myth and archaeology
claims.standfirst: Stones carved with dinosaurs and surgery, said to be ancient. The carver admitted making them.

claims.title: The Ice Cream Machine
claims.standfirst: McDonald's ice cream machines break constantly, and it is a franchise-wide joke. The machines are made by one company, their error codes are proprietary, and the repair rules are the story.

claims.title: Beyond the Ice Wall
claims.standfirst: If the world continues past Antarctica, the continent is not a continent but a boundary — and the treaty that governs it becomes a cover story.

facts.Composite of: Flat Earth rim + hollow Earth doorway
facts.Actual finding: Bunger Hills — a real ice-free oasis
facts.Related: Flat Earth, Hollow Earth, Hidden civilizations

claims.title: IIT versus Global Workspace
claims.standfirst: One theory says consciousness is integrated information, wherever it occurs. The other says it is information broadcast widely in the brain. Both made predictions, and both were tested.

facts.Outcome: Mixed support for both, no winner
facts.Main criticism: Φ cannot be computed for real brains

claims.title: The Illuminati
claims.standfirst: A Bavarian enlightenment society, banned in 1785, has become the supposed secret government of the world. The real organisation lasted nine years and left a paper trail.

claims.title: Illusionism
claims.standfirst: The claim that consciousness as people describe it — the felt quality of experience — is an illusion produced by the brain. It is a serious position and it is hard to state without sounding absurd.

facts.Main objection: An illusion of experience requires experience

claims.title: The Implicit Association Test
claims.standfirst: A reaction-time test said to measure unconscious bias. It correlates weakly with behaviour and its test-retest reliability is poor, which is a problem for a measure used in training and policy.

claims.title: Incognito Was Not Private
claims.standfirst: Private browsing does not stop websites, employers or networks from seeing what you do. A lawsuit forced the clarification.

facts.Does not: Hide activity from networks or sites

claims.title: Genetics and Caste
claims.theme: The ancient world, myth and archaeology
claims.standfirst: Ancient DNA and modern genomes show structure, endogamy and steppe ancestry. The findings are documented and often misread.

claims.title: The Silence of the Indus Script
claims.theme: The ancient world, myth and archaeology
claims.standfirst: A script on thousands of seals from a major civilisation, and no bilingual text to unlock it.

claims.title: Inflation versus a Bounce
claims.standfirst: Inflation is the standard answer to 'why is the universe so uniform?' — and it is also the theory its critics say can explain almost anything, which is the problem.

claims.title: The Inner Core's Spin
claims.standfirst: The solid iron ball at the centre of the planet may rotate slightly differently from the rest of it. The claim rests on subtle differences between earthquake waves recorded decades apart, and the disagreement is about the data as much as the physics.

facts.2023 finding: Rotation may have slowed or paused
facts.Obstacle: Signal at the limit of resolution

claims.title: The Inscribed Square Problem
claims.standfirst: Every closed curve contains four points forming a square. It is easy to state, proved for smooth curves, and open in general.

claims.title: The Interface Theory of Perception
claims.standfirst: The claim that perception is a desktop interface, useful but not true, and that evolution optimises for fitness rather than accuracy. It is a serious argument in the philosophy of perception with an empirical claim that has been contested.

facts.Claim: Perception is a fitness-tuned interface, not a window
facts.Objection: Fitness usually requires tracking real features
facts.Testability: Poor, in the form usually stated

claims.title: The Internal Ramp
claims.theme: The ancient world, myth and archaeology
claims.standfirst: A proposal that the Great Pyramid was built using an internal spiral ramp rather than external ones. The evidence is argued.

claims.title: Iram of the Pillars
claims.theme: The ancient world, myth and archaeology
claims.standfirst: A city in the Qur'an destroyed for its arrogance, and a byword for a lost city in the desert. A site in Oman has been excavated, and the identification is argued.

claims.title: Iran–Contra
claims.standfirst: The US sold arms to Iran and used the proceeds to fund Nicaraguan rebels, in defiance of an embargo and a congressional ban. It was exposed, investigated and pardoned.

facts.Components: Arms to Iran; funds to the Contras

claims.title: The Iron Pillar of Delhi
claims.theme: The ancient world, myth and archaeology
claims.standfirst: A six-tonne iron pillar from the Gupta period that has barely rusted in 1,600 years. It is not a lost technology; it is phosphorus, and a dry climate.

facts.Cause: Ore chemistry plus a dry climate

claims.title: The Isdal Woman
claims.standfirst: A woman found dead in a Norwegian valley in 1970, with erased labels and multiple passports. She has never been identified.

claims.title: It from Bit
claims.standfirst: Wheeler's proposal that physical reality derives from information. It is a slogan with a programme behind it.

claims.title: Jack Is a Time Traveller
claims.standfirst: The theory that Jack Sparrow is a time traveller, based on his modern mannerisms. It is a reading of a performance, not a plot.

claims.title: The Jantar Mantar
claims.theme: The ancient world, myth and archaeology
claims.standfirst: Stone instruments built to measure the sky to a precision that still works.

claims.title: The Jersey Devil
claims.standfirst: A winged creature said to haunt the Pine Barrens of New Jersey, with a legend about a thirteenth child and a wave of sightings in 1909.

claims.title: Jesus in India
claims.theme: The ancient world, myth and archaeology
claims.standfirst: The claim that Jesus survived the crucifixion and travelled to Kashmir. It rests on a nineteenth-century book and no evidence.

facts.Claim: Jesus lived and died in Kashmir

claims.title: The Jevons Paradox
claims.standfirst: In 1865 William Stanley Jevons observed that more efficient steam engines increased Britain's coal consumption, not reduced it. The pattern has been embarrassing energy policy ever since.

facts.Mechanism: Efficiency lowers effective price, raising use
facts.Policy lesson: Efficiency plus a cap, not efficiency alone

claims.title: John Titor
claims.standfirst: A forum poster in 2000 claimed to be a time traveller from 2036. His predictions failed, his physics did not work, and the posts have been traced to a group of people.

facts.Origin: Traced to a group of people

claims.title: Kailasa Carved Downward
claims.theme: The ancient world, myth and archaeology
claims.standfirst: A temple cut from the top of a hill downward, removing everything that is not the building. The method is documented by the marks left behind.

claims.title: Kane Pixels' Backrooms
claims.standfirst: A YouTube series that turned an imageboard joke into a film. It is fiction, made by a named creator, and it has a studio deal.

claims.title: Kanye Quest 3030
claims.standfirst: A fan-made role-playing game with a hidden room that led players to a real website and a recruitment pitch for a 'clone' cult.

claims.title: Kardashev Bottlenecks
claims.standfirst: If growth continues at any plausible rate, the Milky Way is a few tens of millions of years of work. The galaxy is 13 billion years old. The silence is a statement about bottlenecks.

facts.Hardest limit: Waste heat, visible in the infrared

claims.title: Kardashev IV and Omega
claims.standfirst: The scale of civilisations by energy use, extended far past anything observable.

claims.title: The Kardashev Scale
claims.standfirst: A three-step classification of civilisations by energy use, invented for a Soviet radio astronomy paper. It measures nothing we can observe, and it is used constantly as though it did.

facts.What it is not: A measurement, or an observed progression

claims.title: Karin Catherine Waldegrave
claims.standfirst: A Wikipedia editor whose article about an invented painter became a real artwork, and a real exhibition.

claims.title: Keanu Is Immortal
claims.standfirst: The joke that Keanu Reeves has not aged because he is immortal, supported by portraits that look like him. The portraits are a selection, and the joke is the point.

claims.title: The Kensington Runestone
claims.theme: The ancient world, myth and archaeology
claims.standfirst: A Minnesota farmer found a stone in 1898 claiming a Norse expedition reached the American interior in 1362. Runologists have been unanimous for a century that the inscription is nineteenth-century Swedish.

facts.Language: Nineteenth-century Swedish forms, not fourteenth-century Norse
facts.Found by: Olof Öhman, a Swedish immigrant farmer

claims.title: The Kerala School
claims.theme: The ancient world, myth and archaeology
claims.standfirst: A school of mathematicians in Kerala who derived infinite series for trigonometric functions centuries before Europe.

claims.title: Kessler Syndrome
claims.standfirst: Enough collisions in low orbit could produce a cascade that makes the region unusable for centuries. The mechanism is real; whether the cascade has started is argued.

claims.title: Kevin Is Jigsaw
claims.standfirst: The theory that the boy in Home Alone grew up to be the killer in Saw. It is a joke that got elaborate, and it is not in either film.

facts.Claim: Kevin grows up to be Jigsaw

claims.title: Kirby as Cosmic Horror
claims.standfirst: The theory that the pink character's games are secretly about an eldritch being. The lore is real; the horror framing is a reading.

claims.title: Kitty Genovese and the Bystander Effect
claims.standfirst: A murder said to have been witnessed by 38 people who did nothing. The number was wrong; the effect is real but smaller.

claims.title: The Klerksdorp Spheres
claims.theme: The ancient world, myth and archaeology
claims.standfirst: Grooved stone spheres from a South African mine, three billion years old, were said to be manufactured. They are concretions, and the grooves are where crystals grew.

claims.title: Knossos
claims.theme: The ancient world, myth and archaeology
claims.standfirst: The Minoan palace excavated by Arthur Evans, reconstructed in concrete, and argued about ever since.

claims.title: The Kraken
claims.standfirst: A sea monster described by Norwegian writers, and a possible reference to the giant squid. The animal is real; the identification is inference.

claims.title: Kubrick Confessed to the Moon Hoax
claims.standfirst: A video appears to show Stanley Kubrick confessing to faking the Moon landings. The video is a hoax, the interview is real and unrelated, and the claim has been circulating since 2015.

facts.Independent evidence: Orbital images of the sites; retroreflectors

claims.title: Kumari Kandam
claims.standfirst: A lost Tamil landmass said to have sunk south of India, sometimes linked to Lemuria. The ocean floor has been mapped, and there is no continent there.

facts.Tradition: Tamil literary references to a southern land

claims.title: The Kuznets Curve
claims.standfirst: Inequality rises with development and then falls. The data behind it were thin and the pattern is not general.

claims.title: The Labyrinth of Hawara
claims.theme: The ancient world, myth and archaeology
claims.standfirst: A vast mortuary complex described by Herodotus and Strabo, of which only fragments survive.

claims.title: The Laffer Curve
claims.standfirst: Tax revenue is zero at 0% and at 100%, so somewhere in between it peaks. The shape is argued.

claims.title: Lake City Quiet Pills
claims.standfirst: A website and a Reddit thread that appeared to be a front for something. The documents are real; the interpretation is not settled.

claims.title: Lake Nyos
claims.standfirst: A crater lake in Cameroon released a cloud of carbon dioxide that killed about 1,700 people overnight. It is the clearest documented case of a limnic eruption.

claims.title: The Location of Punt
claims.theme: The ancient world, myth and archaeology
claims.standfirst: Egypt traded with a land called Punt for a thousand years, and its location has never been fixed. The candidates run from Somalia to Yemen.

facts.Favoured: African side of the southern Red Sea

claims.title: The Larger Globe
claims.standfirst: “Larger globe” is not one theory. It is at least three, with different inventors, different evidence and different fates.

facts.Leading voices: S. Warren Carey, Ott Hilgenberg, James Maxlow, Giancarlo Scalera
facts.Central claim: Ocean crust is added but not equally destroyed, so the planet grows
facts.Key test: Space geodesy of Earth’s radius (NASA, 2011): no significant change
facts.Related: Hollow Earth, Ice Wall, Giants in the fossil record

claims.title: Last Thursdayism
claims.standfirst: The universe was created last Thursday, complete with your memories, the fossils, and this website. It is not a claim anyone believes. It is a machine for showing what evidence cannot do.

claims.title: The Lavon Affair
claims.standfirst: Israeli military intelligence recruited Egyptian Jews to bomb Western targets in Egypt, in an attempt to damage relations with the West. The operation was exposed, and the political fallout lasted a decade.

claims.title: Lazar and Element 115
claims.standfirst: A man who said he worked on alien craft at Area 51 claimed their fuel was element 115, unknown at the time. Element 115 was synthesised in 2003, and it decays in milliseconds.

claims.title: Lead and Crime
claims.standfirst: Violent crime fell through the 1990s in every rich country at once, and nobody predicted it. One explanation is that a generation stopped breathing leaded petrol as children.

claims.title: Leaky Gut
claims.standfirst: The claim that increased intestinal permeability allows bacterial products into the blood and drives systemic disease. The permeability is measurable; the disease claims are much larger.

claims.title: Lean Mass Hyper-Responders
claims.standfirst: A subgroup on low-carbohydrate diets shows large rises in LDL cholesterol while remaining lean and metabolically healthy. Whether that is harmless is the question.

facts.Features: High LDL, high HDL, low triglycerides, lean
facts.Question: Is the LDL risk the same?

claims.title: Learning Styles
claims.standfirst: The idea that children learn better when taught in their preferred mode — visual, auditory, kinaesthetic — is one of the most widely held beliefs in education and one of the most thoroughly tested negatives in psychology.

facts.Tested claim: The meshing hypothesis, not modality preference
facts.Key review: Pashler et al., 2008, Psych. Science in the Public Interest
facts.Finding: No adequate evidence of a crossover effect

claims.title: Left Brain, Right Brain
claims.standfirst: The idea that people are logical or creative by hemisphere. The hemispheres do differ, and not like that.

claims.title: Why Ten Per Cent Are Left-Handed
claims.standfirst: Hand preference is stable, partly heritable, and not explained. Identical twins disagree about a third of the time, which rules out a simple genetic account.

facts.Twin discordance: Roughly a quarter to a third of identical pairs

claims.title: Legendre's Conjecture
claims.standfirst: There is always a prime between n² and (n+1)². It has been checked far out and proved nowhere.

claims.title: Ley Lines
claims.theme: The ancient world, myth and archaeology
claims.standfirst: Straight lines drawn between ancient sites, said to be channels of earth energy. They are drawn after the fact.

facts.Claim: Ancient sites align on straight lines

claims.title: The Liar's Dividend
claims.standfirst: Deepfakes do not need to fool anyone to do damage. Their existence lets the guilty deny real evidence as fake — and the studies find that it works.

facts.Mechanism: Plausible deniability created by synthetic media

claims.title: Libor Rigging
claims.standfirst: Traders manipulated the interest rate that underpinned trillions in loans and derivatives, by submitting figures that suited their books.

claims.title: The Library of Alexandria
claims.theme: The ancient world, myth and archaeology
claims.standfirst: The greatest library of the ancient world, and the most over-explained destruction in history. It declined over centuries, and no single fire ended it.

claims.title: Life on Mars First
claims.theme: The ancient world, myth and archaeology
claims.standfirst: The claim that life appeared on Mars before Earth, and came here on a rock. The mechanism is possible; the evidence is not there.

claims.title: Life Under the Ice
claims.standfirst: Lakes beneath Antarctica's ice sheet have been sealed for millions of years. Drilling them is a test of whether life persists in isolation.

claims.title: Light's Momentum in Matter
claims.standfirst: Does a photon's momentum in a medium follow Minkowski's or Abraham's formula? The argument ran for a century.

claims.title: Light Speed as a Clock Limit
claims.standfirst: The claim that the speed of light is not a physical constant but the processing limit of a simulation. The constant is measured; the simulation is an interpretation.

claims.title: Liminal Spaces as the Afterlife
claims.standfirst: An aesthetic of empty corridors, read by some as a glimpse of what comes after. The images are real; the reading is fiction.

claims.title: The Lindy Effect
claims.standfirst: At Lindy's delicatessen in New York, comedians believed a joke that had lasted a week would last another week. Mandelbrot gave the observation a name; Taleb gave it a following.

claims.title: Linear A
claims.theme: The ancient world, myth and archaeology
claims.standfirst: The script of Minoan Crete, used for accounting and ritual, and never deciphered. Linear B was cracked because a scholar guessed the language; Linear A has no such handle.

facts.Used: Crete and the Aegean, c. 1800–1450 BC

claims.title: Linguistic Relativity
claims.standfirst: Does the language you speak shape what you can think? The strong version is dead; the weak version has small, replicated effects that are easy to overstate.

facts.Weak form: Language influences attention and memory — supported

claims.title: Linking the Fire
claims.standfirst: The choice at the end of a game about cycles. It is a reading of a fiction, and the fiction is about reading.

facts.Choice: Link the fire or let it fade

claims.title: Little Albert
claims.standfirst: A baby conditioned to fear a white rat. The study is famous, the child was never identified, and the ethics were appalling.

claims.title: The Lobotomy
claims.standfirst: Tens of thousands of brains operated on with an ice-pick-like instrument. The rise and fall are both documented.

claims.title: Local 58
claims.standfirst: A series of fictional emergency broadcasts, made as analog horror. The format borrows the authority of public information films.

claims.title: Nessie as a Giant Eel
claims.theme: Anomalies, fringe science and the unexplained
claims.standfirst: Environmental DNA sampling of Loch Ness found eel DNA in most samples and no reptilian DNA at all. The eel hypothesis is the most parsimonious one on offer, which is not the same as evidence for a giant eel.

facts.Found: Eel DNA at nearly every site; no reptile DNA
facts.What it argues against: A breeding population of large reptiles
facts.Method limit: Rare animals shed too little DNA to detect

claims.title: The London Hammer
claims.theme: The ancient world, myth and archaeology
claims.standfirst: A hammer found encased in rock, said to be 400 million years old. The rock is a concretion that formed around a nineteenth-century tool, which is what the tool is.

facts.Claimed age: 400 million years — for the rock, not the tool

claims.title: The Lonely Runner Conjecture
claims.standfirst: Runners on a circular track at different constant speeds: each will at some point be far from all the others. It is proved for small numbers of runners and open beyond.

facts.Statement: Each runner is lonely at some time

claims.title: The Longyou Caves
claims.theme: The ancient world, myth and archaeology
claims.standfirst: Twenty-four hand-cut caves in China, with no record of who made them or why. The absence of documentation is the puzzle.

claims.title: Loop Quantum Gravity
claims.standfirst: A theory in which space itself is quantised into a network of finite loops. It is mathematically developed, predicts almost nothing measurable, and is one of the two main attempts at quantum gravity.

claims.title: The Los Lunas Stone
claims.theme: The ancient world, myth and archaeology
claims.standfirst: A boulder in New Mexico inscribed with the Ten Commandments in Hebrew, said to be ancient. The inscription is modern.

claims.title: The Lost City of Z
claims.standfirst: A British explorer vanished looking for a civilisation in the Amazon. The civilisation turned out to be real — but not as a city of stone.

claims.title: Lost Continents
claims.standfirst: Lemuria was invented to explain where lemurs came from. Within twenty years it was a civilisation of telepathic giants who kept dinosaurs as pets. The real drowned continents are stranger in a quieter way.

claims.title: Lost Cosmonauts
claims.standfirst: The claim that the Soviet Union lost cosmonauts in orbit and covered it up, based on amateur radio recordings. The archives opened, and the crews are accounted for.

claims.title: The Lost Dutchman Mine
claims.standfirst: A German prospector is said to have found a fabulously rich gold mine in the Superstition Mountains and died without revealing it. People have died looking, and nothing has been found.

facts.Claim: A very rich gold mine, location secret

claims.title: The Lost Ten Tribes
claims.theme: The ancient world, myth and archaeology
claims.standfirst: Ten tribes deported by Assyria and never heard from again, and centuries of claims about where they went.

claims.title: Lucid Dreaming
claims.standfirst: People can know they are dreaming while asleep, and say so from inside the dream. That was verified with eye movements in 1980, which makes it one of the few dream claims with a laboratory receipt.

facts.Verified: LaBerge et al., 1980, by eye-movement signals in REM
facts.Prevalence: About half have one; roughly a fifth monthly
facts.Induction: MILD, WBTB, reality testing — modest, replicated effects
facts.Distinct from: Dream control, which is much less reliable

claims.title: Lumon's Board Is Kier
claims.standfirst: A theory that the mysterious Board in Severance is the company's founder, still directing the firm. It is a reading of the show's theology.

claims.title: The Lunar Wave
claims.standfirst: Videos show a ripple crossing the Moon's face. The claim is a hologram or a projection. The explanation is the atmosphere, the camera, and the way a bright edge behaves in a turbulent sky.

facts.Claim: The Moon is a projection; the wave is a refresh

claims.title: The Lycurgus Cup
claims.theme: The ancient world, myth and archaeology
claims.standfirst: A Roman glass cup that looks green in reflected light and red in transmitted light. It does this with gold and silver nanoparticles, which is nanotechnology by accident, fifteen centuries early.

facts.Effect: Green in reflection, red in transmission

claims.title: Lyonesse
claims.standfirst: A sunken kingdom off Cornwall, drowned in a single night, from which Tristan came. It is literature, and the sea floor has been surveyed.

claims.title: Consciousness in the Machine
claims.standfirst: Whether a system can be conscious is not a question anyone can currently answer, and that is the finding: the tests measure behaviour, and behaviour is compatible with no inner life at all.

facts.The obstacle: The hard problem is unsolved for brains

claims.title: MAD Stability
claims.standfirst: Mutual assured destruction is the most consequential theory ever adopted without a controlled test. It has one data point in its favour and dozens of near-failures against.

claims.title: The Madden Curse
claims.standfirst: Athletes on the cover of the Madden NFL game are said to be injured the following season. The hit rate is high until you count the seasons that went fine.

facts.Base rate: High injury rate in the sport

claims.title: Magnetic Monopoles
claims.standfirst: Cut a magnet in half and you get two magnets. Nobody has ever found an isolated north pole. That absence is one of the most informative null results in physics.

facts.Lab quasiparticles: Spin ice, 2009 — real but not fundamental

claims.title: Magnetoreception
claims.standfirst: Animals navigate by the Earth's magnetic field. That much is settled by decades of behavioural experiments. How a biological cell measures a field a hundred thousand times weaker than a fridge magnet is not.

facts.Behaviour: Robust across birds, fish, reptiles, insects, bacteria
facts.Rival mechanism: Magnetite crystals; induction in marine animals
facts.Field strength: ~50 µT, about 1/200 of a fridge magnet

claims.title: Majestic 12
claims.standfirst: A set of documents supposedly signed by Truman, establishing a secret committee on recovered alien craft. The FBI examined them and called them fake, and the forgery is not subtle.

claims.title: Male Loneliness
claims.standfirst: Surveys find that a substantial share of men report no close friends and rely on a partner for emotional support. The pattern is documented; the explanations are contested.

facts.Key figure: About 15% of men report no close friends

claims.title: The Man from Taured
claims.standfirst: A traveller at a Japanese airport whose passport was from a country that does not exist. The story has no source, and it is an urban legend.

facts.Claim: A passport from a nonexistent country

claims.title: The Mandela Catalogue
claims.standfirst: An analog horror series about 'alternates' replacing people. The name borrows the Mandela effect, and the fiction is explicit.

claims.title: The Mandela Effect
claims.standfirst: A large group of people remember the same wrong thing. It is either evidence of a parallel universe, or the most ordinary fact about human memory there is.

facts.Named after: A false memory of Mandela's death

claims.title: The Manna Machine
claims.theme: The ancient world, myth and archaeology
claims.standfirst: A 1978 book argued that the manna of Exodus was produced by a machine the Israelites carried. The argument is built on a medieval mystical text, and there is no machine in the archaeological record.

claims.title: Mantle Plumes
claims.standfirst: Hot rock rising from deep in the mantle is the standard explanation for Hawaii and Iceland. The seismic evidence for the plumes is weaker than the theory requires.

claims.title: Many Worlds
claims.standfirst: This is the one entry in the archive that is not a fringe claim at all. It is a serious, taught, published interpretation of quantum mechanics — and it still does not mean what the internet says it means.

claims.title: Marble Hornets
claims.standfirst: A YouTube series presented as found footage, made by three people, and one of the founding works of the Slender Man mythos.

claims.title: Marine Ice Cliffs
claims.standfirst: The claim that tall ice cliffs at the edge of Antarctica could collapse rapidly, raising sea level faster than models allow. Later work suggests the cliffs are stronger than the hypothesis assumed.

claims.title: Mario 3 Is a Stage Play
claims.standfirst: A fan theory holds that Super Mario Bros. 3 is staged as a theatre performance — the curtain, the blocks on stands, the card at the end. It is a reading, and the developers have answered it.

facts.Reading: The game is a stage play

claims.title: Market Efficiency
claims.standfirst: If prices already contain all available information, nobody can beat the market except by luck. Half a century of tests has produced both support and a list of exceptions that refuse to go away.

claims.title: Markovian Parallax Denigrate
claims.standfirst: Hundreds of Usenet posts in 1996 containing strings of words with no meaning. The posts are archived; their purpose is not known.

claims.title: The Marshmallow Test
claims.standfirst: Children who waited for a second sweet did better later in life. The correlation replicated weakly, and it is mostly about the family.

claims.title: Marvel's Doom Pivot
claims.standfirst: Marvel cast Robert Downey Jr. as Doctor Doom after playing Iron Man. The decision is documented; the reasoning is the studio's.

claims.title: Mass Hysteria
claims.standfirst: Four hundred people danced until they collapsed in Strasbourg in 1518. The municipal records survive. This is the best-documented case in history of a symptom spreading through a crowd faster than any pathogen.

claims.title: Mast Cell Activation Syndrome
claims.standfirst: A proposed condition in which mast cells release mediators inappropriately, producing flushing, pain and allergic-type symptoms. The cells are real; the syndrome's criteria are contested.

claims.title: Match.com's Fake Messages
claims.standfirst: A dating service that sent messages from fake accounts to lure users back. The regulator documented it.

claims.title: Matrioshka Brains
claims.standfirst: A computer the size of a solar system, built in nested shells that each use the waste heat of the one inside. It is a thought experiment about thermodynamics, and nothing in the sky looks like one.

facts.Principle: Nested shells running on waste heat
facts.Status of the claim: A thought experiment, not an observation

claims.title: The Max Headroom Incident
claims.standfirst: Two Chicago television stations were hijacked by a masked figure in 1987. Nobody was ever charged.

claims.title: Maya Blue
claims.theme: The ancient world, myth and archaeology
claims.standfirst: A pigment that survived a thousand years of tropical rain, and whose chemistry was only explained in the twentieth century.

claims.title: The Maya Tracked Venus
claims.theme: The ancient world, myth and archaeology
claims.standfirst: Maya astronomers recorded the movements of Venus with an accuracy that took European astronomy centuries to match. The tables survive in the Dresden Codex.

claims.title: McDonald's Monopoly Rigging
claims.standfirst: The promotional game was rigged for years by the man who ran its security, who sold the winning pieces. The FBI investigation is documented.

claims.title: MeatSleep
claims.standfirst: A creepypasta told through a series of unsettling videos and posts. It is fiction, and the format is the work.

claims.title: Mechanistic Interpretability
claims.standfirst: The attempt to reverse-engineer what a model is computing inside. Results are documented; the general claim is not.

claims.title: The Median Voter Theorem
claims.standfirst: Duncan Black proved in 1948 that majority voting on a single dimension picks the median voter's preference. Downs applied it to parties in 1957. The prediction is convergence, and the last forty years of American politics is the counter-example.

facts.Empirical record: Convergence in some systems, divergence in others

claims.title: Medusa
claims.theme: The ancient world, myth and archaeology
claims.standfirst: The gorgon's head turns viewers to stone. Explanations have included fossils, masks and ritual, and none is established.

claims.title: The Megafauna Extinctions
claims.standfirst: Large animals disappeared from every continent except Africa at the end of the Pleistocene. Climate, humans, or both — and the answer differs by continent.

claims.title: Megalodon in the Trench
claims.standfirst: A giant shark known from teeth, extinct for millions of years, said to survive in the deep ocean. The size of the animal is the argument against it.

claims.title: The Memory of Water
claims.standfirst: A claim that water retains the properties of substances diluted out of existence. The experiment failed a supervised test.

claims.title: The Men in Black
claims.standfirst: Men in dark suits who visit witnesses and warn them to keep quiet. The stories are consistent, old, and unsupported by a single verified case.

claims.title: The MH370 Portal Video
claims.standfirst: A video said to show the missing aircraft disappearing into a portal. The video is a composite.

claims.title: Mica in the Pyramids
claims.theme: The ancient world, myth and archaeology
claims.standfirst: A claim that mica sheets in Egyptian monuments served an electrical purpose. Mica is present; the electrical use is not.

claims.title: The Michigan Relics
claims.theme: The ancient world, myth and archaeology
claims.standfirst: Thousands of inscribed objects 'found' in Michigan, said to record ancient migrations. They were made and planted.

claims.title: Microbiome Forensics
claims.standfirst: The bacteria on a body or a phone may identify a person or a place. The research is early.

claims.title: Microplastics and Hormones
claims.standfirst: Microplastics are everywhere, including in blood and placentas. Whether they act as endocrine disruptors in people is a question the exposure data cannot yet answer.

claims.title: Miguel Never Came Back
claims.standfirst: A theory that a character's journey ends in death rather than return. It is an interpretation of a film.

claims.title: Milgram's Obedience Studies
claims.standfirst: The experiments that seemed to show ordinary people would follow orders to hurt strangers. The archives complicate the result.

claims.title: Mind Uploading
claims.standfirst: Scan a brain at sufficient resolution, run the simulation, and the person continues in software. The proposal has a serious engineering roadmap and no working example, and the philosophical problem is not the engineering.

facts.Achieved: No mammalian whole-brain scan at that resolution
facts.Open: Whether the emulation is the person

claims.title: Minimum Wage Effects
claims.standfirst: New Jersey raised its minimum wage in 1992 and Pennsylvania did not. The study that compared them overturned a textbook, and every study since has been arguing with it.

facts.Moderate increases: Small employment effect in most studies
facts.Large increases: Measurable job losses in low-wage brackets
facts.CBO, 2019: $15 floor: big raises, modest job losses

claims.title: The Minotaur as Earthquake
claims.theme: The ancient world, myth and archaeology
claims.standfirst: A claim that the Minotaur myth encodes a memory of the Thera eruption or of Cretan earthquakes. The myth is real; the encoding is a proposal.

claims.title: Mirror Matter
claims.standfirst: Every particle could have a mirror twin in a hidden sector that interacts only gravitationally. It would be dark matter, and it would be invisible. It is an elegant idea with no detection.

facts.Proposed: Lee and Yang, 1956; developed by Foot, Volkas and others
facts.Claim: A hidden sector coupled only gravitationally
facts.Tests: Photon and neutron mixing experiments — null

claims.title: Mirror Neurons
claims.standfirst: Neurons that fire both when a monkey acts and when it watches the same action. They were found in macaques, and the human claims built on them — empathy, language, autism — are much larger than the evidence.

claims.title: Mithras and Precession
claims.theme: The ancient world, myth and archaeology
claims.standfirst: A claim that Mithraic iconography encodes the precession of the equinoxes. The imagery is real; the astronomy is a reading.

claims.title: Model Collapse
claims.standfirst: Training on model output is said to degrade models. The phenomenon is documented in some settings; the generality is argued.

facts.Claim: Training on synthetic data degrades models

claims.title: Model Welfare
claims.standfirst: The question of whether AI systems can suffer. The question is serious; the evidence is absent.

claims.title: Modern Monetary Theory
claims.standfirst: A government that borrows in a currency it prints can always pay. That is arithmetic, not ideology. What follows from it — and what does not — is where the fight is.

facts.Core claim: A currency issuer cannot involuntarily default

claims.title: The Dancing Girl of Mohenjo-daro
claims.theme: The ancient world, myth and archaeology
claims.standfirst: A bronze figurine from the Indus cities, and a name that tells you more about its finders than its subject.

claims.title: The Mohenjo-daro Blast
claims.theme: The ancient world, myth and archaeology
claims.standfirst: A claim that an ancient city was destroyed by an atomic blast. The 'evidence' is a scattered set of bones and a misread verse.

claims.title: Mokele-mbembe
claims.standfirst: A large animal said to live in the Congo basin, often described as a sauropod dinosaur. Expeditions have been going for a century and have produced stories, not specimens.

claims.title: The Momo Panic
claims.standfirst: A bird-woman image was said to be contacting children on WhatsApp and instructing them to harm themselves. It was a sculpture, a hoax, and a lesson in how a panic travels.

facts.The claim: A character contacting children and urging harm

claims.title: MOND
claims.standfirst: One constant, 10⁻¹⁰ metres per second squared, and a rule: below that acceleration, gravity pulls harder than Newton says. It fits galaxies beautifully and clusters badly.

claims.title: The Mongolian Death Worm
claims.standfirst: A worm said to live in the Gobi, capable of spitting venom or electricity. The reports come from travellers, and no specimen has ever been produced.

claims.title: Monopoly's Anti-Monopoly Origin
claims.standfirst: The world's most famous property game was invented to teach that land monopolies are unjust. The irony is documented in patents and in the inventor's own words.

claims.title: Monsanto's Ghostwritten Studies
claims.standfirst: Internal documents showed the company drafting research on its own products and arranging for academics to publish it.

claims.title: The Montauk Project
claims.standfirst: A claimed secret programme at a decommissioned radar station on Long Island: mind control, time travel, and a boy who conjured a monster. The station is real; the programme exists only in books.

claims.title: The Monument Mythos
claims.standfirst: An analog horror series in which American monuments are something other than monuments.

claims.title: How the Moon Formed
claims.standfirst: A Mars-sized body hit the young Earth and the debris became the Moon. The broad picture is accepted; the isotope evidence has been making it complicated for twenty years.

facts.Key problem: Lunar and terrestrial isotopes nearly identical

claims.title: The End of Moore’s Law
claims.standfirst: Moore's law was an observation about economics that became a schedule the industry organised itself around. Its end is not the end of computing; it is the end of a very specific kind of free progress.

facts.Concentration: Very few firms at the leading edge

claims.title: The Moving Sofa Problem
claims.standfirst: The largest sofa that can be moved round a right-angled corridor. The best known answer has stood since 1992 and is not proved optimal.

claims.title: The Mozart Effect
claims.standfirst: Listening to Mozart was said to raise IQ. It raises arousal for about fifteen minutes, and the IQ claim was a press release that outlived the paper.

facts.Original finding: A short-term spatial task boost after ten minutes of Mozart

claims.title: The Mpemba Effect
claims.theme: Anomalies, fringe science and the unexplained
claims.standfirst: Hot water sometimes freezes faster than cold. It was reported by a Tanzanian schoolboy in 1963, dismissed by his teacher, and is still argued about by physicists with better equipment and no agreement on what would count as an answer.

facts.What would settle it: One definition, one protocol, many labs

claims.title: Mr Blue Eyes
claims.standfirst: A minor character read as the series' hidden controller. It is an interpretation of a game.

claims.title: MSG Syndrome
claims.standfirst: A letter to a medical journal created a condition. Blinded trials did not find it.

claims.title: Multiple Intelligences
claims.standfirst: The claim that intelligence comes in eight or nine independent kinds reshaped classrooms worldwide. As a description of how abilities are organised it does not survive the data, and the theory was never built to be tested.

facts.Psychometric evidence: A general factor plus narrower abilities, not eight independents
facts.Testability: The taxonomy was not derived from data and makes no failing prediction

claims.title: The Multiverse
claims.standfirst: The proposal that our universe is one of many. It follows from some theories and has no direct test.

claims.title: The Muon's Wobble
claims.standfirst: For twenty years the muon's magnetic moment looked like the cleanest crack in the Standard Model. Then a different way of doing the hardest part of the calculation closed the gap.

facts.Quantity: Anomalous magnetic moment of the muon, g−2
facts.Complication: Lattice QCD versus e+e− data disagree

claims.title: Muppet Citizenship
claims.standfirst: A joke that the Muppets are legally citizens with rights. It is a joke about puppets, and it is filed as one.

claims.title: The Mushroom War
claims.standfirst: Adventure Time is set a thousand years after a nuclear war, and the show reveals it slowly. The backstory is documented in the episodes, not invented by fans.

claims.title: Mutants & “Superpowers”
claims.standfirst: There are people whose bones will not break, people who can see a colour you cannot, and populations that function where visitors vomit and lose consciousness. None of them glow.

claims.title: MyHouse.wad
claims.standfirst: A Doom level released with a story about a friend who died. It is a work of art in a 1993 game engine, and it is fiction.

claims.title: Unknown Mysteries
claims.standfirst: Two case studies in how a mystery is manufactured: a loose boundary, a good story, a bestseller — and then, thirty years later, the paperwork.

facts.Best reading: Water and fertility ritual; routes and gathering

claims.title: The Mystery Flesh Pit
claims.standfirst: A worldbuilding project about a national park inside a living organism. It is fiction, presented as an archive of a place that never existed.

claims.title: N-Rays
claims.standfirst: A French physicist discovered a new radiation that only he could detect. It did not exist.

claims.title: Nan Madol
claims.theme: The ancient world, myth and archaeology
claims.standfirst: A city built on artificial islets from stacked basalt columns, in a lagoon in Micronesia. It is real, and it took centuries.

claims.title: Navier–Stokes Existence and Smoothness
claims.standfirst: The equations that describe fluid flow are used every day and have never been proved to have solutions that stay smooth. Turbulence is the reason it matters.

facts.Question: Smooth solutions for all time in 3D?

claims.title: Nazca Lines as Runways
claims.theme: The ancient world, myth and archaeology
claims.standfirst: The lines and figures on the Nazca desert were said to be landing strips for aircraft. They are shallow scrapes in the surface, and the ground beneath them would not support a wheel.

claims.title: The Nazca Lines as Water Maps
claims.standfirst: The lines may mark routes to water rather than sky gods or runways. The puquios — spiral wells — are real, and the lines' relationship to them is argued.

claims.title: Near-Death Experiences as DMT Release
claims.standfirst: The claim that the brain releases DMT at death, producing the tunnel, the light and the life review. The resemblance is real; the release has never been measured.

claims.title: Neanderthal Cannibalism
claims.standfirst: Bones from several Neanderthal sites carry cut marks and fractures consistent with butchery. The evidence is direct, and the interpretation is not.

claims.title: Why the Neanderthals Went
claims.standfirst: They lived in Europe for hundreds of thousands of years and disappeared within a few thousand of our arrival. The cause is still argued.

claims.title: Near-Death Experiences
claims.standfirst: People brought back from cardiac arrest report tunnels, light, life review and calm. The reports are real and consistent enough to study. What they mean about death is the part that is not.

facts.Core features: Peace, tunnel, light, life review, figures, a boundary
facts.Key test: AWARE study: hidden targets, no confirmed hit
facts.Leading accounts: Hypoxia, reperfusion, temporal lobe, REM intrusion
facts.What would settle it: Verified perception from a position the body could not occupy

claims.title: Nemo Means Nobody
claims.standfirst: The name in Finding Nemo means 'nobody' in Latin, which is either a coincidence or the film's central joke. The etymology is documented; the intent is not.

claims.title: Neolithic Trepanation
claims.theme: The ancient world, myth and archaeology
claims.standfirst: Skulls with holes cut into them, and bone regrowth showing that some people survived. The surgery is documented; the motive is not.

claims.title: The Nephilim
claims.theme: The ancient world, myth and archaeology
claims.standfirst: Genesis mentions giants called Nephilim in a handful of verses. The enormous literature built on them — bloodlines, hybrids, modern sightings — is later, and the verses are not a description of a species.

claims.title: Nero and the Fire
claims.theme: The ancient world, myth and archaeology
claims.standfirst: Nero was said to have fiddled while Rome burned, and to have started the fire to clear space for his palace. The first is impossible and the second is unlikely.

claims.title: NESARA and GESARA
claims.standfirst: A claimed law that would cancel all debt, abolish income tax and deliver prosperity packages. It has been 'about to be announced' for thirty years.

facts.Claim: A secret law abolishing debt and tax
facts.Structure: Imminent transformation, blocked by a cabal

claims.title: Nessie as a Plesiosaur
claims.standfirst: The Loch Ness Monster is usually drawn as a plesiosaur. That identification has a specific problem: a breeding population of large air-breathing reptiles in a cold lake would leave traces, and none has been found.

facts.Lake: Loch Ness, 56 km², cold and deep

claims.title: New Coke as a Trojan Horse
claims.standfirst: Coca-Cola replaced its recipe in 1985, the public revolted, and the original returned in 79 days. The claim is that the whole thing was a planned manoeuvre.

claims.title: Newgrange and the Solstice
claims.theme: The ancient world, myth and archaeology
claims.standfirst: A passage tomb in Ireland aligned so that the rising sun at midwinter reaches the chamber floor. The alignment is measured every year.

claims.title: The Newport Tower
claims.theme: The ancient world, myth and archaeology
claims.standfirst: A stone tower in Rhode Island said to be a medieval Norse church. The mortar dates it to the colonial period.

claims.title: Nibiru
claims.theme: The ancient world, myth and archaeology
claims.standfirst: A claimed planet on a long orbit that would pass Earth. It has been predicted repeatedly and has never appeared.

facts.Claim: A planet on a long orbit

claims.title: The Ningen
claims.standfirst: A Japanese internet cryptid: a white, humanoid whale said to live in Antarctic waters. It appears to have been invented online.

claims.title: The Ninth Legion
claims.theme: The ancient world, myth and archaeology
claims.standfirst: A Roman legion stationed in Britain disappears from the record, and has been sent to Scotland, annihilated, or transferred. The evidence points to the dull answer.

claims.title: NoEnd House
claims.standfirst: A creepypasta about a haunted house with a series of rooms and no exit. It is fiction, and its structure has been widely copied.

claims.title: Non-Human Biologics
claims.standfirst: A 2023 congressional hearing was told the United States holds craft and biological material of non-human origin. The claim is consequential, the evidence has not been produced, and the official investigations have found nothing to support it.

facts.Official finding: AARO, 2024 — no evidence of extraterrestrial technology

claims.title: Novel Reading and Madness
claims.standfirst: Novels were said to corrupt young women and drive them mad. The claim is documented; the evidence never existed.

claims.title: The NPC Theory
claims.standfirst: The joke-theory that most people are non-player characters with no inner life. It began as a meme, and a survey found a surprising number of people willing to say they doubted others' consciousness.

claims.title: Oak Island
claims.standfirst: A depression in the ground, a story about pirate gold, and 230 years of men bankrupting themselves to find it. The pit is real. The treasure is the part nobody has produced.

claims.title: Oannes
claims.theme: The ancient world, myth and archaeology
claims.standfirst: A Babylonian priest described a fish-man who came out of the sea and taught civilisation. It is a myth recorded centuries after the fact, and it has become a fixture of the ancient-astronaut literature.

facts.Figure: Fish-bodied being who teaches the arts

claims.title: Objective Collapse
claims.standfirst: Standard quantum theory says the wavefunction collapses when measured, and never says what a measurement is. Objective-collapse models replace that with real physics: the collapse happens on its own.

claims.title: Ocean Worlds Are the Norm
claims.standfirst: Europa, Enceladus, Titan, Ganymede, Ceres: subsurface oceans may be common. Whether they are habitable is another question.

claims.title: Odd Perfect Numbers
claims.standfirst: A perfect number equals the sum of its divisors. Every one known is even, and nobody knows whether an odd one exists.

facts.Definition: Equals the sum of its proper divisors

claims.title: Ollantaytambo Machining
claims.theme: The ancient world, myth and archaeology
claims.standfirst: A claim that Inca stonework at Ollantaytambo shows machine cutting. The precision is real; the machines are not.

claims.title: The Olmec Heads as Africans
claims.theme: The ancient world, myth and archaeology
claims.standfirst: The colossal stone heads of the Olmec show faces with broad noses and full lips, and have been said to depict Africans. They depict Olmec rulers, and the stone came from local quarries.

claims.title: The Omega Point
claims.standfirst: Pierre Teilhard de Chardin imagined evolution converging on a collective consciousness he called the Omega Point. Frank Tipler gave it an equation — and the equation needs a universe that is not going to collapse.

claims.title: One Piece and the All Blue
claims.standfirst: A theory about where a legendary sea is. It is an interpretation of a long-running manga.

facts.Claim: The All Blue will be created

claims.title: Open versus Closed Models
claims.standfirst: A closed model can be withdrawn. An open one cannot. That single asymmetry drives most of the argument, and neither side disputes it.

facts.Irreversibility: A published weight file cannot be recalled
facts.Audit argument: Closed models can only be probed via API
facts.Unsettled: The size of the marginal risk

claims.title: Open Weights
claims.standfirst: Models released for anyone to run. The benefits and the risks are both documented, and the argument is live.

claims.title: Operation Highjump
claims.standfirst: A US naval expedition to Antarctica in 1946–47, with 4,700 men and a carrier. It has been read as a military operation against a hidden Nazi or alien base.

claims.title: Operation Snow White
claims.standfirst: The Church of Scientology ran a systematic infiltration of US government offices to remove documents about itself. Eleven senior officials were convicted.

facts.Scale: Largest known infiltration of US government

claims.title: Oppenheimer's Chain Reaction
claims.standfirst: The film dramatises a fear that the first test might ignite the atmosphere. The fear was real, the calculation was done, and the answer was no.

claims.title: Orch-OR
