claims.title: The Watchers of Enoch
claims.theme: The ancient world, myth and archaeology
claims.standfirst: The Book of Enoch describes 200 angels who descended, taught forbidden knowledge and fathered giants. It is apocalyptic literature, and the reading that makes them extraterrestrials is a twentieth-century one.

claims.title: Where Earth’s Water Came From
claims.standfirst: Oceans cover most of the planet, and the planet should have boiled them off while it was forming. Something delivered water afterwards — or it was here all along.

claims.title: The Water-Powered Car
claims.standfirst: The claim that a car can run on water alone, usually by splitting it into hydrogen and oxygen on board. The electrolysis costs more energy than the hydrogen returns.

facts.Claim: A car running on water alone
facts.Problem: Electrolysis costs more than it returns

claims.title: Water Shafts and Locks
claims.theme: The ancient world, myth and archaeology
claims.standfirst: A claim that the pyramid's shafts were part of a hydraulic system. The shafts are real; the water is not there.

claims.title: Webdriver Torso
claims.standfirst: A YouTube channel posted thousands of videos of coloured rectangles and a beep. It was a Google test, and Google said so.

claims.title: The Wet-Bulb Threshold
claims.standfirst: At a wet-bulb temperature of about 35 °C, sweat stops cooling the body and a healthy adult dies within hours, even in the shade. It is a hard physical limit, and parts of the world are approaching it.

facts.Mechanism: Sweat can no longer cool the skin

claims.title: Whale Strandings
claims.standfirst: Hundreds of whales beach themselves together, and the explanations on offer range from sonar to solar storms. Some of them have been demonstrated. Most have not.

facts.Commonest species: Pilot whales, sperm whales, beaked whales
facts.Social mechanism: Pod cohesion: one animal's error becomes the group's
facts.Key evidence: Necropsy: gas-bubble lesions in exposed beaked whales

claims.title: Where Is Kate
claims.standfirst: Weeks of speculation about a public figure's absence, ended by an announcement and a diagnosis. A case study in how rumours fill a vacuum.

claims.title: A White Dwarf as a Weapon
claims.standfirst: The claim that a stellar remnant could be steered, or used, as a weapon. It appears in science fiction and in UFO lore; the physics of moving a star is the objection.

facts.Requirement: Momentum change on a stellar scale

claims.title: White Holes
claims.standfirst: Run the film backwards and a black hole becomes a white hole: a region nothing can enter, spraying matter outward. The equations permit it. The sky has not shown one.

claims.title: Why We Age
claims.standfirst: Ageing is not one process. Several mechanisms are well described, no single one explains it, and the interventions that extend lifespan in mice have mostly failed to translate.

facts.Evolutionary accounts: Mutation accumulation; antagonistic pleiotropy; disposable soma
facts.Mechanistic hallmarks: Nine, including senescence and proteostasis loss
facts.Interventions: Caloric restriction, rapamycin, senolytics — under study

claims.title: Why We Dream
claims.standfirst: Dreams are vivid, emotional, remembered badly, and unexplained. The leading theories disagree about whether they do anything at all.

facts.Theories: Activation-synthesis; threat simulation; memory; social simulation
facts.Documented: REM association; incorporation of recent experience
facts.Limitation: Content known only from waking reports

claims.title: Why We Sleep
claims.standfirst: Sleep restores something, and after a century of research nobody can say precisely what. The candidates are all supported and none is sufficient.

facts.Necessary: Yes; deprivation is harmful and eventually fatal
facts.Candidate functions: Restoration, synaptic homeostasis, clearance, immunity, safety

claims.title: Why We Stood Up
claims.standfirst: Bipedalism is the oldest human trait and the least explained. Several hypotheses compete and none is settled.

claims.title: Why We Yawn
claims.standfirst: Yawning is contagious, appears before birth, and has no agreed function. The brain-cooling account is the best supported; the social account explains the contagion.

claims.title: Will Died in Bel-Air
claims.standfirst: The theory that Will Smith's character died in the first episode and the series is his afterlife. It explains nothing that needs explaining, and it is a joke.

claims.title: WIMPs versus Axions
claims.standfirst: Two candidates for dark matter, decades of experiments, and no detection of either.

claims.title: The Wolfsegg Iron
claims.theme: The ancient world, myth and archaeology
claims.standfirst: An iron block with a groove was found inside a lignite seam in Austria in 1885 and dated to millions of years. It is a piece of nineteenth-century mining equipment.

facts.Dating error: The seam's age applied to the object

claims.title: WorldCorp Enterprises
claims.standfirst: A YouTube channel posting disturbing, disjointed videos with corporate branding. It has never been explained, and it may be art.

claims.title: The Wow! Signal
claims.standfirst: Seventy-two seconds of narrowband radio at the hydrogen frequency, recorded once and never again. It is still the best candidate for a signal from elsewhere, and it is not evidence of one.

claims.title: Xenotransplantation
claims.standfirst: Transplanting pig organs into people. The first living recipients survived weeks to months, which is both a real advance and a long way from a treatment.

claims.title: XKeyscore and Tempora
claims.standfirst: Two bulk-collection programmes disclosed in 2013. Their existence is documented; their scope is partly redacted.

claims.title: The XYY Supermale
claims.standfirst: An extra Y chromosome was said to produce aggressive criminals. The claim collapsed when the sampling was examined.

claims.title: Yamashita's Gold
claims.theme: The ancient world, myth and archaeology
claims.standfirst: The claim that the Japanese army buried billions in looted treasure in the Philippines at the end of the war. Seventy years of digging has produced plaques, tunnels and lawsuits, and no gold.

facts.Claim: Billions in looted treasure buried in the Philippines
facts.Not documented: The hoard, its size, the maps

claims.title: Yang–Mills and the Mass Gap
claims.standfirst: Quantum field theory works, and nobody can prove that its simplest version is mathematically consistent — or that its particles have mass.

facts.Question: A rigorous theory with a mass gap in 4D

claims.title: The Yangshan Stele
claims.theme: The ancient world, myth and archaeology
claims.standfirst: A colossal stone monument left in its quarry, unfinished, still attached at one edge. It is the best evidence of how such monuments were made.

claims.title: YAYVIDEOGAMES
claims.standfirst: A YouTube channel whose strange, looping videos turned out to be made by a person, not a mystery.

claims.title: The Yellow Emperor's Dragon
claims.theme: The ancient world, myth and archaeology
claims.standfirst: The Yellow Emperor is said to have ascended to heaven on a dragon, taking seventy officials with him. It is a foundation myth of Chinese civilisation, and it has been read as a spacecraft.

facts.The motif: Ascent on a dragon at the end of the reign

claims.title: The Yonaguni Monument
claims.theme: The ancient world, myth and archaeology
claims.standfirst: A submerged rock formation off Japan has flat surfaces, right angles and a stair-like structure. Geologists read it as natural sandstone; others read it as a worked monument.

claims.title: You Will Own Nothing
claims.standfirst: A phrase from a marketing essay, read as a policy programme. The essay is real; the programme is not.

claims.title: The Younger Dryas Impact
claims.standfirst: The Younger Dryas cooling is real and abrupt. Whether an impact caused it — and whether that impact explains megafaunal extinctions and the Clovis collapse — is where the argument starts.

claims.title: The Yuba County Five
claims.standfirst: Five men drove into the mountains after a basketball game and were found dead months later. What happened in between has never been established.

claims.title: Zealandia
claims.standfirst: A continent of five million square kilometres, 94% of it underwater, with New Zealand and New Caledonia above the surface. It is real, and it was formally described in 2017.

claims.title: Why Zebras Have Stripes
claims.standfirst: Camouflage, confusion, cooling and social signalling have all been proposed. The hypothesis with the best experimental support is the least romantic one: flies.

facts.Experiment: Striped horse coats, 2019 and 2023: fewer landings
facts.Consensus: Probably several mechanisms, with flies first

claims.title: Zelda's Timeline Convergence
claims.standfirst: The Zelda games are officially split into three timelines that later games merge. The split is documented; the convergence is a fan reading.

claims.title: Zero-Click Search Extinction
claims.standfirst: More searches now end without a click, because the answer appears on the results page or in an AI summary. Whether that is the death of the open web or an ordinary shift is argued.

claims.title: Zero-Point Extraction
claims.standfirst: The claim that usable energy can be drawn from the quantum vacuum. The vacuum energy is real; the extraction is not.

claims.title: Zero and Its Transmission
claims.theme: The ancient world, myth and archaeology
claims.standfirst: The numeral system with place value and zero travelled from India to the world. The route is documented.

claims.title: Zhang Heng's Seismoscope
claims.theme: The ancient world, myth and archaeology
claims.standfirst: A bronze vessel that detected earthquakes and indicated direction. The instrument is described in a text and its principle is understood.

facts.Form: Bronze vessel with dragons and toads

claims.title: Zion Is Another Matrix
claims.standfirst: The theory that the 'real world' in The Matrix is a second layer of simulation. It is an elegant reading, and the filmmakers have described it differently.

facts.Filmmakers: Describe the real world as real

claims.title: The Zodiac Killer
claims.standfirst: Five confirmed murders in California, a set of ciphers sent to newspapers, and a case that has never been closed. Two of the ciphers have been solved.

claims.title: The Zone of Silence
claims.standfirst: A patch of desert in Mexico where radios allegedly fail and meteorites fall. The explanation is an absence of transmitters and a lot of empty space.

claims.title: The Zoo Hypothesis
claims.standfirst: If the galaxy is full of life, why is it quiet? John Ball's 1973 answer was that they are leaving us alone on purpose — treating Earth as a preserve, and waiting for us to grow up.
